They showed the Ustasha, who are superior in manpower, that the Serbian heroism is still alive. The Serbian Chetnik units will be active in all other areas of western Serbia: In Serbian Krajina, in Serbian Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. We shall not give up a single inch of Serbian territory. "Let the Slovenes leave Yugoslavia. They have never been our brothers or friends. Let the Croats go too. Let Croatia secede. But we are not giving them an inch of the territory to the east of the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica line."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Continuing, on May 15, 1991, the accused again warned Serbs of a new genocide threatening them. And this is shown in Exhibit P178, which I'd ask to be played at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Seselj: The Croatian Ustashas are defeated. Vukasin Soskocanin led the resistance in Borovo Selo and Ustashas didn't. "Crowds shouting: Revenge! Revenge! Revenge! "Seselj: It is too much ... we have to get back because the new genocide is threatening us. We have to get back to the old Ustasha politics of Stjepan Mesic. "Crowds shouting: We will kill Mesic! We will kill Mesic! "Seselj: Ante Markovic. "Crowds shouting: Ante Ustasha! Ante Ustasha! Tito Ustasha! Tito Ustasha! "Seselj: It is too much ... Serbs from Serbian Krajina will not remain without help or without protection. "Crowds shouting: Right! Right! "Seselj: Hundreds of thousands ... at any moment ... words, and then to leave, and Serbia to remain definitely damaged, maimed. Serbs will never accept any kind of confederation. We, people in Yugoslavia ... which is above the interest of the Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In that crowd, as the Trial Chamber was able to observe, were men dressed up in military garb and in Chetnik insignia. And after inciting that crowd, his calls for revenge intensified yet. And as his calls for revenge intensified, so did his deployment of Seseljevci to Croatia. The accused described in Exhibit P30 how: "In 1991 we began organising volunteers on a larger scale and sending them to already established front lines, particularly in Eastern Slavonia." The accused's volunteers, his Seseljevci, knew what they were fighting for, for revenge against non-Serbs to create a Greater Serbia. As Vukovar was shelled and right up to the crimes perpetrated there, this increase in volunteer deployment was accompanied by the accused's continued persecution propaganda against non-Serbs. On the 27th of August, 1991, in Exhibit P1279, the accused refers to Ustasha, saying: "We express the decisiveness not to stop the struggle until we liberate all the Serbian lands and until we are completely separated from those who never were our brothers and friends." And he continued this refrain into September of 1991. For example, the accused promised that "the time has come to avenge all the Serb victims and unite all the Serb lands." Exhibit P355. In the same month he described a volunteer dying at "the perfidious hands of the Ustashas." He added: "You will not go unavenged. The foe will feel the punishment of the Serbian people ... the time has come to settle old accounts, the time has come to avenge all Serbian sacrifices and to unify all the Serbian lands." P40. In an issue of "Velika Srbija," the head of the SRS Crisis Staff, Witness Petkovic, said: "... a blood-sucking virus called genocide which is again breeding in the Ustasha blood is threatening the Serbian people with new mass graves, pits, slaughter-houses, jails ... we are facing a new wave of extermination, which even Dr. Mengele would envy." Exhibit P1280. And still in September of 1991, all shortly before the crimes committed in Vukovar, the accused lauded that: "Chetnik weapons have retained their old glory in battles against the Croatian Ustashas so far. They have reason to fear the Chetniks." Exhibit P1182. At the end of September 1991 - now only weeks before the crimes committed in Vukovar - the accused used the freedom of a private session of the National Assembly to set out more clearly his ethnic strategy and to link Serb territorial claims to World War II crimes. "In Croatia only a military solution suits us Serbs. Why? Because the world will never recognise a million of Jasenovac victims, because the world will recognise, after all, if we force them by military force to recognise as Serbian only those territories where there is a Serbian majority, but we also want those territories where Serbs make up between 30 and 50 per cent, as well as those where today there are no Serbs at all thanks to the Second World War genocide because of some strategic reasons. We cannot defend the borders if they are only ethnic borders, if we are not led also by some strategic reasons in determining them ... because the greatest danger for us, that we haven't even discussed yet, is that the world might force us to keep on living with the Croatians and Slovenians in the same country." P1257 at pages 54 to 55. In Vukovar, both the accused and his Seseljevci were notorious. The deployment of Seseljevci after all of these speeches that the accused made was so substantial and so linked to the accused that their units were referred to as Seseljevci even in official JNA communications, as seen in Exhibit P41. In early November 1991, the accused escorted a group of Seseljevci to the Vukovar front lines. The press coverage of his visit, memorialised in Exhibit P1283, highlighted that the accused was a national deputy in the Assembly of Serbia who warned of the "Ustasha hordes who have launched a new genocide against the Serbs in these parts." That's a quote. Addressing the volunteers and members of the TO in Vukovar, he promised: "We will soon send new volunteers. Vukovar must fall quickly, and with the fall of Vukovar, the Ustashas are finished in these parts." His visit had an immediate effect on the Croat forces. "Immediately upon Dr. Vojislav Seselj's arrival on the Ustasha forces' radio waves, a warning was heard: 'Look out, the Chetnik motherfucker Seselj has arrived.'" When he later visited Vukovar, the accused told members of the Serb forces, including perpetrators of the subsequent massacre at Ovcara, that: "No Ustasha should leave Vukovar alive." As Ms. Hochhauser will describe to you, soon after Seseljevci and other members of the Serb forces committed atrocities throughout Vukovar, including at Velepromet and Ovcara. But I'd like to show you now how fighters on the ground were indoctrinated by the accused's goal of cutting deep into Croatia so that Serbs could seize lands all the way up to the KOKV line. And at this time I'd ask that Exhibit P57 be played.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "Journalist: And amongst the horror there is surreal incongruity of celebration. Extremist Serb militia men and women posing triumphantly for an end-of-battle photograph, before returning to a morning feast of music and laughter fuelled by alcohol. "AL: The motto on their flag is 'Freedom or death' and they vow they will fight on. "UMV: No, it's not finished. "AL: What for you do the Serbs need to take before the war is over? "UMV: War will be over when we have our limits Karlobag-Karlovac-Ogulin-Virovitica. All place where Serbian people live must be free, you know. We must clean up with the Croatians."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "We must clean up with the Croatians." After Croats were murdered or expelled, and many villages and towns, like Vukovar, were razed to the ground, the accused celebrated the forced displacement of Croats, making it clear it was the successful implementation of the common purpose. For example, the accused thanked Croats who fled from the once Croat majority Osijek, described as a ghost town in Exhibit P1283. In an interview admitted as Exhibit P1186 he made clear that minority Serb areas would also be cleansed of Croats. "Listen, what does it mean, Serbs are a minority? 30 or 40 per cent of Serbs is a minority? What should we care that they are a minority? This is the territory that has to be part of the Serbian state; among other things, the London Treaty in 1915 stipulated that. A huge number of Croats have already left Osijek, almost 100.000. How nice of them. We should thank them. They have nowhere to return to. Osijek remains a Serb town." This was ethnic cleansing. But in the accused's lexicon, he sanitised ethnic cleansing, calling it a mere "population exchange," the same phrase he'd later use to try to justify his crimes in Hrtkovci. And in quoting that language he also said: "We will never again be able to live side by side with the Croats within the border of the same state." Throughout the conflict in Croatia, as the accused deployed volunteers, he targeted Croatians as Ustashas, labelling them and the Croatian leadership as genocidal. The accused used the term "Ustasha" to denigrate and debase all Croats as murderous threats to Serbs, cheapening their lives and justifying their destruction. In his brief, the accused claims that the term "Ustasha" is now used by Croats and that he never denigrated all Croats as Ustasha. This is wholly unsupported by the evidence before the Trial Chamber. The evidence beyond a reasonable doubt shows that this accused evoked the powerful symbolism of World War II Chetniks to frighten and mobilise Serbs and that this accused also labelled all Croats as Ustashas to invoke the memories of fascist atrocities committed against Serbs during that war and to depict all Croats as a present-day threat. VS-004 testified at transcript pages 3380 and 3624 that: "The word 'Ustasha,' among all Serbs, is the worst thing you can mention because throughout their history it was the Ustasha who committed the greatest crimes against Serbs ... it's something that exists as the worst in the world, as an executioner." The 1990 political platform of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, admitted as Exhibit P27, referred to a "new Ustasha leader" who had emerged in Croatia with "a new genocidal policy" against Serbs. The SRS 1991 platform repeated this language. The evidence shows that the accused intended to press the volatile issue of the responsibility of the Croatian people for the Ustashas' crimes committed in World War II. This was to link Croats to those who committed past crimes against Serbs and to justify crimes against them. During the lead-up to the war in Croatia, the accused explicitly conveyed that he viewed all Croats as Ustasha. In Exhibit P34, for example, he said: "How is one supposed to negotiate with the Ustashas? Did you see today that the Croatian people are entirely Ustasha? There are very few exceptions." In a televised interview, admitted as Exhibit P31 [sic], he made it very clear, he made it very simple, and he said: "Croats must be punished." In a radio interview in January 1992, admitted as Exhibit 1189, the accused bragged that his volunteers helped to destroy "pure Croatian villages," as they were all considered "strong Ustasha fortifications." He warned his listeners that "Croats exist as a people on the basis of an anti-Serb hatred." According to him, they and Slovenes were ready to become part of the Fourth German Reich. Without distinguishing civilians and combatants, Ustashas from Croats, he reported to the listening audience that "Croats were dying in masses." And several months later he physically committed persecution against the Croats of Hrtkovci, changing that village from a Croat majority village into a Serb majority one. His intent throughout, from the crimes in Croatia to the crimes in Hrtkovci, was to denigrate Croats and incite crimes against them, including forcing them to leave and destroying them. As Mr. Marcussen described, by early 1992, the JCE members were shifting their focus from Croatia to Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accused began his persecution campaign there well before open conflict started. His pounding, unrelenting, hateful, and divisive language helped to prepare the ground for the discriminatory violence against non-Serbs. With increasing frequency, the accused threatened bloodshed in BiH. He invoked blood over and over and over again to foreshadow the consequences of BiH's declaration of independence. As early as November 1991, around the time that Karadzic made his highway to hell speech, the accused in Exhibit P1186, in a radio interview announced "there would be rivers of blood" if BiH declared independence. So if Bosnian Muslims refused to remain part of a truncated Yugoslavia, the accused threatened: "Bosnia will be part of the Serbian state." On the 16th of January, 1992, in Exhibit P1190, the accused in another radio interview told his audience that "Bosnia and Herzegovina had nowhere to go," so "Muslims were now clutching at straws," according to him. And even if Muslims stayed in a state with the Serbs and were given autonomy, the accused by his calculations said that they were entitled to just 18 per cent of BiH, although they were the largest ethnic group. And in that radio interview he glorified Serbs as born soldiers, taught "military skills in the cradle," who should be feared by non-Serbs. On the 20th of February, 1992, the accused used a televised SRS press conference, admitted as P1192 and P395, to repeat his ultimatum to Bosnian Muslims that, should BiH seek independence, there would be flooded rivers of blood there. The accused hosted this press conference with Mirko Blagojevic, president of the regional boards of both the SRS and SCP for north-eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina and whom the accused later appointed later appointed Vojvoda. Less than two months later, Blagojevic participated in the take-over and crimes in Bijeljina. As war drew closer, the accused's persecution propaganda in BiH intensified. In publicised speeches, rallies, and interviews throughout March 1992, the accused pounded his audience. He pounded Serbs, he pounded Bosnian Muslims, and he pounded them with three themes. First, the accused insisted that Serbs had the right to dominate most or all of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as described, for example, in P1293, where he said this in front of a rally of approximately 6- to 7.000 people held on March 1st. Second, he claimed that Serbs in BiH were under threat because if BiH became independent, Serbs would have to live under an "Islamic Jamahiriya" governed by "Islamic fundamentalists" and "Turks." As described in Exhibits P1193, 1293 and 1295. Third, the accused made it clear that Serb control over BiH would require a civil war and massive bloodshed. For example, Exhibit P1324 describes a press conference held on March 5th. In that press conference, the accused threatened and intimidated Bosnian Muslims and directed Serb forces about what should happen when BiH declared independence. He promised "bloodshed." He promised a "bloody civil war." And he promised "rivers of blood" flowing in BiH. To contribute to that bloody war, he publicly directed the SRS and SCP throughout rump Yugoslavia "to put our volunteers on the highest alert so that they are ready at any moment to intervene in areas in BiH." And that can be found at page 1 of that exhibit. And similarly, Exhibit P1293 from March 6th, the same day that BiH declared independence, the accused used the same hateful language. And he pounded these oratorical trigger points in his audience again and again and again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I understood the Trial Chamber correctly, we are going until 7.00; is that correct? Thank you. On the 26th of March, mere days before Serb take-overs in BiH commenced, the accused, in Exhibit P685, used inflammatory language to condition Serbs to discriminatory violence against non-Serbs and to make non-Serbs fearful. [As read] "The independence of BiH can be achieved only at graveyards through, blood running knee-deep, in the territory which the Serbian people have vital interests ..." He announced he and the SRS did not recognise the Presidency of BiH and he welcomed the creation of separate Serb authorities, a critical preparation for implementing the common criminal purpose. And he made it clear: "Serbs will never allow the Islamic Jamahiriya to extend to their people." The accused's propaganda continued unabated. He addressed the media and/or the National Assembly almost every day in early April 1992, and he demonised non-Serbs, as seen in, among other exhibits, those listed in footnotes 45, 1803, 1804, and 1807 of the Prosecution's closing brief. On April 1st, 1992, Serb take-overs in BiH began. A little over a week later, on 9 April 1992, the accused held a press conference, Exhibit 685, with Mirko Blagojevic. Vojvoda Blagojevic was already being questioned by the press about the killing of civilians in Bijeljina. Standing next to Blagojevic, the accused praised him as commander of the Seseljevci who had initiated the take-over in Bijeljina. He called upon Serbs to defend Republika Srpska from "Ustasha and pan-Islamist hordes." The accused repeated his refrain and repeated his refrain about protecting Serbian territories against the threat of Islamic fundamentalism. In Exhibit P396, he repeated that the Serbian people in BiH would never recognise "this new Jamahiriya and will never give up its territories." He also repeated and reinforced his inciting calls to Serbs to support the criminal campaign in BiH. For example, as the brutal take-over of Zvornik was executed by Serb forces, the accused reminded them, in Exhibit P1195, "it has been up to us for a long time now to help," help Serb forces in Zvornik with men and other support. The accused did not halt his propaganda or calls for violence as the criminal campaign in BiH escalated. Instead, he used his influence and authority to promote unification of all Serb lands and to create a climate of ethnic fear and hatred. He justified or ignored the crimes that had already been committed, thereby preparing the ground for further criminality. For instance, on the 28th of May, 1992, non-Serbs were being tortured and murdered at the Ekonomija Farm and Ciglane factory in Zvornik. The accused stood before a large rally crowd and promoted cleansing the BiH side of the Drina River. Accompanied by Nikola Poplasen, president of the SRS BiH, and Rade Leskovac, president of the SRS Krajina, the accused told the applauding crowd that: "The only thing that remained to be done in Bosnia and Herzegovina is to clean up the left bank of the Drina, secure a corridor between the Bosnian Krajina and Semberija, and liberate the Serbian part of Sarajevo, while the rest is already in our hands." Exhibit P1200. On the 28th of May, 1992; the 4th of June, 1992; and the 11th of June, 1992, the accused --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection. I don't want to interject and interrupt Ms. Biersay. Something has been omitted from the transcript. The date of the rally where I was seen with Poplasen and Leskovac. She did mention the date but now I'm looking at the transcript and I can't see the date, and I believe that this should be corrected. It is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... indicate what the date of that meeting was with Nikola Poplasen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It is published in Exhibit P1200 and it's dated the 28th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is impossible. There is a two- or even three-year difference, it's impossible, and I suppose that's why the date was omitted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Biersay, could you please verify the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I would be happy to do that for Your Honours. After the accused gave those press conferences on May 28th, 4th of June, and 11 June, 1992, where he continued to pound Muslims, two days later, after the 28th of May, 1992, press conference, between the 30th and 31st of May, 1992, a group of Seseljevci murdered 88 non-Serbs at Drinjaca Dom Kulture in Zvornik. On June 4, the accused lamented that Serbs had already suffered under Turkish rule for 500 years and repeated his territorial goal of the KOKV line. On the following day, Serb forces, including a group led by Seselj's Vojvoda Vidovic, murdered 22 non-Serb men and women in Ljesevo, Ilijas. June 11th, 1992, was just a few days after 740 non-Serbs had been massacred in Karakaj and Gero's slaughter-house. While non-Serbs were being tortured and murdered in Celopek Dom Kulture in Zvornik, the accused again made the inflammatory claim that Bosnian Muslims were trying to return Serbs to 500 years of "Turkish slavery." The accused's predictions of rivers of blood flowing in BiH had foreshadowed the brutal crimes committed there. Serb forces carried out his call to make parts of BiH into a slice of Greater Serbia. Of course, words were not all that the accused deployed, he also pounded Croatia and pounded BiH with other weapons, the volunteers he mobilised throughout the crime bases. I see that we have, I think, reached the end of the session, so before continuing the next section I wonder if the Trial Chamber would be happy to stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since Ms. Biersay has finished, maybe she could tell us the date of the rally which I attended together with Poplasen and Leskovac. I suppose that she has had the time to find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Biersay, if you haven't found the date, you can tell us the date tomorrow morning. But in any case, I will also verify in Exhibit P1200 in order to check what you said. We shall be here again tomorrow at 9.00 a.m., and I wish you all a good night. Until then.
